newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds stable, waiting game nearly over.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds stable, waiting game nearly over.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were reasonably stable going into the weekend with the market fully focussed on next week's policy making meetings in both Australia and the U.S.
*Some analysts see benefits for local debt in the dollar bloc.
Australian bond yields were reasonably stable going into the weekend with the short end marginally softer ahead of the policy making meetings in both Australia and the U.S.

There has been a long waiting game for the Reserve Bank board meeting since the May labour force data suggested that another monetary policy easing could be on the cards, although these expectations have wavered in the past few sessions.
As one analyst put it: "The next direction for the market is really down to the authorities next week."
Reuters monthly interest rate poll of economists gave a 52.5 percent chance of an easing in July and a 50 percent chance of a cut thereafter if nothing happens next month.

May motor registrations showed a 0.7 percent fall after a revised 1.5 percent drop in April. The data, normally ignored by the market, added to the argument that consumer demand currently remains weak and that a policy easing is needed to fuel growth.

Chris Caton, Bankers Trust's chief economist, said the data showed that the economy remains flat. While he thought it was unlikely that the RBA would cut next week, he gave a better than even chance of an easing after the August board meeting.

Yield differentials tightened sharply to Canada after the Bank of Canada's surprise 25 basis points tightening on Thursday. Conversely, spreads widened to New Zealand after the RBNZ endorsed a larger than expected loosening in monetary conditions in its Monetary Policy Statement.
